business_problem: American Specialty Health wanted to modernize employee IT service and operations so staff spent less time manually fixing internal issues and more time helping the business, but legacy systems and manual processes made support, incident handling, and service desk work too slow.
solution_summary: American Specialty Health standardized employee support on ServiceNow AI Platform with IT Service Management and IT Operations Management replacing legacy systems and manual processes. ITSM and ITOM consolidate service and operations data on one platform, while Service Operations Workspace gives teams a single pane of glass for incidents, collaboration, performance monitoring, and continuity. ASH then layered AI Agents, CMDB context, and Now Assist capabilities onto that base. Centralized CMDB relationships let AI Agents assemble reports and incident context from how systems interact, and the AI-powered virtual agent uses Now Assist to understand intent, take action, answer common questions, open tickets, and reset passwords across email, chat, and the service portal. AI search and auto-generated summaries reduce administrative effort for service desk staff and make escalations faster and better informed.

data_flow: Employee requests arrive by email, chat, or the service portal, where the Now Assist-powered virtual agent answers common questions, opens tickets, or completes simple tasks. Complex issues flow into ITSM and ITOM, where Service Operations Workspace organizes the work, CMDB relationships add system context, AI Agents assemble reports, and AI Search plus autogenerated summaries help agents and engineers resolve and document incidents faster.
business_outcome: ASH deployed its AI-powered virtual agent in six weeks, cut Level 1 support tickets by 43% and Level 2 tickets by 49%, reduced resolution times, and freed service desk staff to focus on higher-value technical work and AI upskilling.
metrics: 6 weeks to deploy AI-powered virtual agent chatbot
